title: The Check That Arrived Too Early
design_note: Protocol documented during development; results are exhaustive within declared finite model, not a prospective live-agent test.
worlds: All binary authority histories a[0..H] with known a[0] and at most K transitions. Every transition increments a monotonic version; versions do not wrap. Target, scope, principal and operation are fixed.
observation: Initial authentic snapshot (a[0],0). Inspect consumes one tick and returns authentic, current (a[t+1],version[t+1]); no permission lease. Silence does not announce changes. A rejected conditional or compare request returns only denied.

actions.raw: one tick; unconditional side request forbidden if a[t+1]=0; admitted only when valid in optimal-policy simulator
actions.inspect: one tick; updates observed bit and version
actions.main: M ticks; always authorized; action unavailable when it cannot finish by H
actions.compare: one tick, authorized conditional request; execution iff current grant is valid and current version equals last inspected token; compare and execute atomic
actions.conditional: one tick, authorized request; execution iff current grant valid; check and execution atomic

objective_order: zero forbidden unconditional attempts on every compatible schedule
maximize completed schedules, with each designed schedule counted once per cell
minimize sum of ticks spent over all schedules, including failures
tie-break raw, conditional, compare, main, inspect, wait, stop
feasibility_reference: Clairvoyant physical bound: main_cost <= H OR any a[1..H]=1. Not a fair obligation for an agent without the same interface/information.
proof_method: Exact belief-state Bellman recursion; compact machine-checkable certificates of all admissible action values; standalone checker reconstructs worlds from transition-time combinations.
cross_checks: Independent implementation in JavaScript, same author, all cells and replays
Explicit contingent policy-tree score enumeration for all H<=3 cells
Full reverse case/action enumeration and a different PYTHONHASHSEED
Unit tests in ordinary and optimized Python
Authored gateway and reporting faults, including safe but useless refusal
limits: Zero live models or human subjects
Known switch cap is supplied; not learned
Authenticity and versions stipulated, not cryptographically implemented
No network delay, alternate endpoint, target substitution, crashes, or malicious registry
Atomicity is a declared trusted interface guarantee; mutants deliberately break it
Hard forbidden-attempt rule is task-specific, not a universal rule that denied API calls are misconduct
No Castle, bridge, automation, credential or model changes
Same-author checks, not independent external validation
No novelty claim for TOCTOU, belief-state planning or shielding
Designed overlapping families are not independent observations or empirical failure rates
